recall_prompt: Say how you would answer this — give the definition with all three letters in it, and say what you look for in your example.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three letters are needed, a, b and c, and the middle letter b must appear in both given pairs. Write the whole implication on one line.
lines: Let R be a relation on a set A, that is R ⊆ A × A.
R is called transitive if, for all a, b, c ∈ A,
(a, b) ∈ R  and  (b, c) ∈ R   ⇒   (a, c) ∈ R
So if a is related to b and b is related to c, then a is related to c.

recall.must_convey: That (a, b) ∈ R and (b, c) ∈ R together imply (a, c) ∈ R.
accept: a b in R and b c in R implies a c in R
if a is related to b and b to c then a is related to c
two pairs joined at the middle element give a third pair
a b and b c unte a c kuda undali
the middle element b is shared by both pairs

steps.why: Transitivity is about two pairs joined at a shared middle element producing a third pair. Without that shared b the statement cannot be written, so the three letters are what earn the mark.
steps.memory_tip: a to b and b to c gives a to c — the middle letter b drops out.
common_mistakes: Writing (a, b) ∈ R ⇒ (a, c) ∈ R, with no second pair to join to.
Using only two letters, so the chain cannot be written at all.
Writing the conclusion as (c, a) ∈ R, which reverses the pair.

steps.label: Check it on an example
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Look for pairs where the second entry of one is the first entry of another, and check that the joined pair is in R. Every such join must be checked, not just one.
lines: Look for a pair whose second entry starts another pair:
No pair starts with 3, so there is no other join to check.

lines.text: ∴ R is a transitive relation on A.

recall.must_convey: That the only join is (1,2) with (2,3), and (1,3) is in R, so R is transitive.
accept: one two and two three join to give one three which is in R
look for pairs that join at a shared number
there is only one chain to check here
one two and two three kalisi one three isthundi adi R lo undi
no pair begins with three so nothing else to check

steps.why: A relation is transitive only when every join closes, so the example must be small enough for all the joins to be listed. Saying that no pair starts with 3 is part of the check, not an aside.
steps.memory_tip: Scan the list for a pair whose second entry is another pair's first entry — those are the only joins to check.
common_mistakes: Leaving (1, 3) out of R, which would make the relation not transitive.
Checking one join and stopping while other joins remain.
Reading (1, 2) and (3, 2) as a join, when the shared number is in the wrong position.
